title: Measure and Improve Reranker Calibration for Low-Resource Prompt Sets
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: reduce reranker quality regressions and increase signal fidelity for small customer prompt sets while preserving endpoint latency and throughput. Background: we see noisy NDCG/MRR measurements when evaluating customer prompt sets with <200 queries per split, leading to churn in A/B rollouts and spurious alerts. This ticket scopes a combined instrumentation + evaluation strategy: (1) add stratified statistical hooks for low-volume prompt sets, (2) compute debiased NDCG/MRR confidence intervals, (3) create automated pairwise calibration checks and alerting, and (4) wire lightweight A/B traffic decorators to collect per-customer ground truth labels and clicks where available. We must also validate that added telemetry has negligible impact on p95 latency and does not increase token costs materially.
tasks: Design new eval harness that supports stratified sampling and bootstrap NDCG/MRR variance estimates
Implement server-side A/B instrumentation headers and sample keys for per-customer promptset grouping
Add calibration metrics: score distribution histograms, reliability diagrams, and expected calibration error (ECE) computation
Integrate bootstrapped confidence interval calculations into ranking dashboards
Create migration plan to enable per-tenant rerank caches with TTL heuristics for low-frequency promptsets
End-to-end tests: synthetic workload to validate telemetry and check <2ms median added latency
Prepare rollout playbook and opt-in feature flag for customers to provide label feedback
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows stratified NDCG@10 and MRR with 95% bootstrap CI for each customer promptset
Calibration ECE reduced by at least 10% on internal benchmark tocks over baseline
A/B instrumentation does not increase p95 latency by more than 5% on staging
Per-tenant embedding cache reduces cold-start latency for low-volume promptsets by >=20%
Unit and integration tests added; PR merged and run on CI; rollout gated behind feature flag
